content: Filamin-binding LIM protein 1 (FBLIM1) is a protein encoded by the FBLIM1 gene in humans. This protein contains several distinct structural domains, including an N-terminal domain that binds to filamin, a central proline-rich domain, and multiple LIM domains located at the C-terminal region. FBLIM1 is primarily localized at cell junctions, where it is thought to serve as a molecular link between cell adhesion structures and the actin cytoskeleton. It is believed to play a critical role in the assembly and stabilization of actin filaments. Additionally, FBLIM1 is implicated in regulating various cellular processes, such as cell adhesion, cell morphology, and cell motility. Beyond its cytoplasmic functions, FBLIM1 is also found in the nucleus. Within the nuclear environment, it may influence cardiomyocyte differentiation by interacting with the CSX/NKX2-5 transcription factor. Alternative splicing of the FBLIM1 gene results in the production of multiple transcript variants, which encode different isoforms of the protein. FBLIM1 has been experimentally shown to interact with several other proteins, including Filamin, PLEKHC1, and FLNB. These interactions suggest that FBLIM1 participates in complex protein networks that regulate cellular architecture and function.
